A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROVA/PVRBench work and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–I. The shorter bibliography in v2 shifts appendix pagination without removing scientific material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on PVRBench, ablations, qualitative examples, and training-time measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 2 evaluations, Figure 5 ablations, and Appendix G timing measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same corruption generation, difficulty-aware selection, memory replay, dual-branch GRPO optimization, and reward definitions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Video-R1-derived training data and PVRBench, VisBench, and UrbanVideo evaluations, covering the same indoor/outdoor tasks and perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Tables 2–4 and 15 and the appendix comparisons, including Video-R1, Embodied-R, proprietary models, and alternative reward judges.

E3.justification: The reported training budgets, model sizes, frame counts, perturbation procedures, evaluation metrics, and experimental controls remain unchanged in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same component, masking, and reward ablations; hyperparameter and frame-count analyses; curriculum diagnostics; and qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix G.2 retains the three-run training-ratio measurement description, and Table 13 retains identical timing variability reporting. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All matched numerical results and qualitative findings are retained. For example, Table 2 reports Qwen2.5-VL-7B average perturbed accuracy of 0.33 and its ROVA variant's 0.47 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Appendix G cost proposition and proof, Appendix H reward analysis, and Appendix I statistical-manifold assumptions and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about ROVA, PVRBench, perturbation robustness, and transfer to clean benchmarks.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning binary rewards, fixed weighting, judge dependence, and holistic reasoning feedback.

D1.justification: Implementation details, prompt templates, hyperparameters, hardware, timing information, dataset-construction documentation, and the displayed project-page access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 omits the WorldMM reference by Yeo et al. (2026), leaving '?' at its corresponding Section 2 citation. The remaining related-work argument and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Reference entries receive editorial revisions, including expanded MVBench author/venue details, a changed publication description for VideoMultiAgents, and removal of many publication fields. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Shortened reference entries reflow the bibliography and slightly alter spacing on page 11; appendix contents-page numbers and pagination update accordingly. Figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 provides fuller MVBench attribution and a more compact bibliography, but removes WorldMM's entry and leaves an unresolved '?' in Section 2. With scientific content and evidence unchanged, the decisive effect is a small decline in citation completeness and editorial reliability.
